messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: p99 latency exceeded SLO on /v1/generate (dedicated pool: eu-west-1-dedicated-3). Current p95=340ms, p99=2.1s, streaming stalls observed. Trigger: latency_thresholds: p99>1.5s

Priya (oncall): seeing it. paging Jonah and Ava. any immediate customer impact?

Jonah (sre): yes, multiple customer dashboards show elevated end-to-end latency and TCP backpressure in the service tier. Some streaming requests time out at consumer side. No 500 spike yet but queue depth at pool is climbing.

Ava (infra): visual confirms queue depth on the dedicated pool nodes -> queue_depth = 130 -> usually < 20. Autoscaler logs show scale events queued but warmup lagging. Looks like warmup latency (gpu init + model load) ~110s.

Priya (oncall): ok, priority=P1. immediate mitigation options? can we failover traffic to a different pool or to hosted fallback model?

Miguel (runtime): we have compatible model variant on hosted and another dedicated pool in eu-west-1 (dedicated-1). Two constraints: 1) cross-pool routing needs a short window to update routing table (estimated 30-60s), 2) fallback to hosted will increase cost and might change latency characteristics but avoids stalls.

Jonah (sre): recommended plan: 1) throttle new long-running streaming sessions for non-critical customers, 2) start routing 30% of traffic to hosted fallback, 3) manually add 4 GPUs to eu-west-1-dedicated-3 and pre-warm model on those nodes, 4) enable short-circuit prefix cache for hot prompts.

Priya (oncall): do it. Ava, can you add capacity manually? Miguel, can you prepare warmup job and cache enable? I'll inform CS for customer comms.

Ava (infra): running manual scale:```
dedicated-cli scale-pool --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3 --add-gpus 4 --reason "incident: p99 latency"
```
Scale accepted, creating 4 instances. kube events show pods scheduling. Note: images still pulling on two nodes. ETA ~90-140s.

Miguel (runtime): prepping warmup job:```
# synthetic warmup to prime KV and model caches
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://eu-west-1-dedicated-3.internal/v1/generate -d '{"input":"warmup prompt","max_tokens":8}' &
done
```
Will run once nodes are ready. Also toggling prefix cache for model-id: rwd-gpt-xl:```
redwood-cli cache set --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3 --model rwd-gpt-xl --mode prefix --ttl 600
```

Priya (oncall): Jonah, can you start routing change? we want gradual 30% -> 70% if stable.

Jonah (sre): updating routing policy:```
redwood-routing set-policy --service generate --region eu-west-1 --split "dedicated-3:70,dedicated-1:0,hosted-fallback:30" --dry-run=false
```
Applied. Monitoring for error rate and latency.

(2m later) Ava (infra): new nodes Ready. Starting warmup job now.

Miguel (runtime): warmup rate 50r/s distributed across nodes. KV cache hit starts climbing from ~2% -> ~48% after 30s. p95 trending down to 180ms, p99 trending down to 1.2s. Streaming stalls still occasional.

Priya (oncall): CS notified. Sending short note: "We are mitigating a latency incident affecting select dedicated pools in eu-west-1; we've added capacity and routing fallbacks; streaming stalls may be intermittent; working to restore SLOs."

PagerDuty Bot: Incident acknowledged by Priya. On-call handoff scheduled in 2h.

Jonah (sre): Observability notes: tail latencies correlate with burst arrivals from one customer (acct: alpha-analytics) — large batched streaming sessions that spike queue length. Suggest applying per-customer rate limits and burst smoothing.

Priya (oncall): can we throttle that tenant temporarily?

Ava (infra): applying token bucket limiter on tenant alpha-analytics at 20r/s:```
redwood-tenant-limit set --tenant alpha-analytics --rate 20 --burst 40
```
Applied. After throttle, incoming queue depth drops ~45%. p99 drops below 900ms.

Miguel (runtime): enabling stream keepalive tweaks to reduce stall duration, pushing patch to runtime config:```
runtime-config set --streaming keepalive_interval=10s --streaming reconnect_timeout=6s
```
Patch applied, rollout 50% -> 100% in 2 minutes.

(10m later) Jonah (sre): metrics: p95=120ms, p99=430ms, stream stall errors down 85%. Queue depth stable < 10. No 5xx seen. Looks like mitigation successful.

Priya (oncall): great. still keep routing split at 70/30 for another 15 minutes then re-evaluate. Miguel/Ava please record the warmup time and autoscaler lag for postmortem.

Miguel (runtime): noted. autoscaler events: scale decision -> resource provisioning duration: median 94s, model load time median 110s. Will add to incident log. Also seeing cold-start penalty for quantized weights on new nodes; may need pre-provisioned hot pool for burst handling.

Jonah (sre): immediate action items assigned: Miguel -> runtime warmup optimization + investigate pre-warmed standby pool (owner); Ava -> autoscaler tuning and quicker image pull (owner); Priya -> customer comms + incident blameless postmortem writeup (owner).

Priya (oncall): handing off to Jonah who will own the incident for next 2h while I switch to follow-up comms. Jonah, take it.

Jonah (sre): taking over. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate if p99 creeps above 1s. On-call next up: Sam in 2h. Sam please prepare to join if needed.

Priya (oncall): thanks everyone, good mitigation. will file summary and RCA notes later. :white_check_mark:

(incident thread ends)
